questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which structure is present in all viruses?
questions.hint: Some viruses lack an envelope.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement about viral genetic material is correct?
options: It is either DNA or RNA
It is always both DNA and RNA
questions.answer: It is either DNA or RNA
questions.hint: Viruses are classified partly by their type of nucleic acid.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for a virus that infects bacteria.
questions.hint: The name means 'bacteria eater'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which of these do viruses lack?
questions.hint: They depend on the host for energy and synthesis.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Viruses are described as obligate ___ parasites. Fill in the missing word.
questions.hint: Think about where they must be to reproduce.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for a complete virus particle outside a host cell.
questions.hint: It is the infectious form.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: At the end of the lytic cycle, the host cell usually…
options: integrates the viral DNA into its chromosome
questions.hint: 'Lysis' means splitting.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the viral DNA once it has been integrated into a bacterial chromosome during the lysogenic cycle.
questions.hint: The word contains 'phage'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which enzyme do retroviruses use to make DNA from their RNA genome?
questions.hint: The process runs opposite to transcription.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Where does the envelope of an enveloped virus come from?
options: The host cell membrane, as the virus buds out
questions.answer: The host cell membrane, as the virus buds out
questions.hint: It is a phospholipid bilayer with viral glycoproteins inserted.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What can cause a prophage to switch from the lysogenic to the lytic cycle?
options: Stress to the host, such as DNA damage by UV light
questions.answer: Stress to the host, such as DNA damage by UV light
questions.hint: The prophage 'leaves' when the host seems threatened.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which hypothesis proposes that viruses arose from pieces of host genetic material that escaped from cells?
questions.hint: The name describes genes leaving a cell.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why do influenza vaccines often need updating?
options: High mutation rates change the virus's surface antigens
Humans lose all memory cells each year
questions.answer: High mutation rates change the virus's surface antigens
questions.hint: Consider how quickly RNA viruses evolve.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which observation supports the idea that viruses have several separate origins?
options: Viruses show very great diversity of genomes and structures with no gene shared by all
All viruses share the same capsid gene
questions.answer: Viruses show very great diversity of genomes and structures with no gene shared by all
questions.hint: A single origin would leave a common signature.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Compare and contrast the lytic and lysogenic cycles of a bacteriophage.
questions.hint: Include at least one similarity and the fate of both the viral DNA and the host cell.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss the evidence for different hypotheses about the origin of viruses.
questions.hint: Consider the progressive, regressive and virus-first ideas, and what evidence fits each.

bio-sl.topic: Data handling: statistical tests and graphs in biology

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of graph is most suitable for showing the relationship between two continuous variables?
questions.hint: Each point represents one pair of measurements.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of graph is most suitable for comparing the mean height of plants grown in three different soils?
options: Line graph with a trend line
questions.hint: The independent variable is categorical.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: On a bar chart of mean values, error bars most commonly show…
questions.hint: They show the spread of the data around the mean.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Calculate the mean of these leaf lengths in mm: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.
questions.hint: Add them and divide by how many there are.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant's mass increased from 40 g to 50 g. Calculate the percentage increase.
questions.hint: Divide the change by the original value, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is a t-test used for?
options: Testing whether the means of two samples differ significantly
Measuring the strength of a correlation
Drawing a line of best fit
questions.answer: Testing whether the means of two samples differ significantly
questions.hint: It compares two groups.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the null hypothesis in a t-test comparing two samples?
options: There is no significant difference between the means
The data are not normally distributed
questions.answer: There is no significant difference between the means
questions.hint: 'Null' suggests nothing is happening.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which significance level is most commonly used in biology?
questions.hint: It corresponds to 5%.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Calculate the degrees of freedom for an unpaired t-test with sample sizes of 10 and 12.
questions.hint: Use n₁ + n₂ − 2.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The calculated t value is 3.45 and the critical value at p = 0.05 is 2.09. What should you conclude?
options: Reject the null hypothesis: the difference is significant
Accept the null hypothesis: the difference is not significant
questions.answer: Reject the null hypothesis: the difference is significant
questions.hint: Compare the calculated value with the critical value.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: If the error bars (standard deviation) of two means overlap a lot, this suggests that…
options: the difference between the means is probably not significant
questions.answer: the difference between the means is probably not significant
questions.hint: Overlap means the data ranges are similar.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A correlation coefficient of r = −0.92 indicates…
questions.hint: Look at both the sign and the size.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which correlation coefficient shows the weakest correlation?
questions.hint: The closer to zero, the weaker.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for when a change in one variable directly produces a change in another.
questions.hint: It is stronger than correlation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Ice cream sales and cases of sunburn are positively correlated. What is the best explanation?
options: A third variable, sunny weather, increases both
Sunburn causes people to buy ice cream
The correlation must be a calculation error
questions.answer: A third variable, sunny weather, increases both
questions.hint: Look for a factor that affects both variables.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why a strong correlation between two variables does not prove that one causes the other. Use an example.
questions.hint: Consider third variables and what kind of investigation could show causation.
